about: Authored query pairs on Employees for tools/sample_db_bench.py. label: 'equivalent' or 'different' under the declared keys minus 'drop' (not_null:T.c, pk:T, fk:T.c). A 'different' pair carries a witness: 'real' (the two queries already differ on the Employees data) or a small database (missing columns are completed with legal values) that satisfies the remaining declarations and separates them. 'sibling' names the pair it negates. The database has one nullable column (titles.to_date) and composite keys with DATE columns (titles: emp_no, title, from_date; salaries: emp_no, from_date), so the key-dependent siblings are about those. Most queries carry a filter on emp_no so that their results on the 3.9 million real rows stay small; it is part of both sides of every pair.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: dept_emp.emp_no is NOT NULL and references employees' key: every assignment joins exactly one employee
pairs.left: SELECT de.emp_no, de.dept_no FROM dept_emp AS de JOIN employees AS e ON de.emp_no = e.emp_no WHERE de.emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, dept_no FROM dept_emp WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the foreign key an assignment may name an employee that does not exist
pairs.left: SELECT de.emp_no, de.dept_no FROM dept_emp AS de JOIN employees AS e ON de.emp_no = e.emp_no WHERE de.emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, dept_no FROM dept_emp WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without employees' key two employees may share a number, and the join repeats the assignment
pairs.left: SELECT de.emp_no, de.dept_no FROM dept_emp AS de JOIN employees AS e ON de.emp_no = e.emp_no WHERE de.emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, dept_no FROM dept_emp WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: salaries.emp_no references employees' key and is NOT NULL, so each salary joins exactly one employee
pairs.left: SELECT s.emp_no, s.from_date, s.salary FROM salaries AS s JOIN employees AS e ON s.emp_no = e.emp_no WHERE s.emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, from_date, salary FROM salaries WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the foreign key a salary may belong to no employee
pairs.left: SELECT s.emp_no, s.from_date, s.salary FROM salaries AS s JOIN employees AS e ON s.emp_no = e.emp_no WHERE s.emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, from_date, salary FROM salaries WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: both parents are joined on their keys through NOT NULL foreign keys, so neither join changes the rows
pairs.left: SELECT de.emp_no, de.dept_no FROM dept_emp AS de JOIN employees AS e ON de.emp_no = e.emp_no JOIN departments AS d ON de.dept_no = d.dept_no WHERE de.emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, dept_no FROM dept_emp WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the foreign key to departments an assignment may name a department that does not exist
pairs.left: SELECT de.emp_no, de.dept_no FROM dept_emp AS de JOIN employees AS e ON de.emp_no = e.emp_no JOIN departments AS d ON de.dept_no = d.dept_no WHERE de.emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, dept_no FROM dept_emp WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: dept_manager.dept_no is a NOT NULL foreign key (a string key) to departments
pairs.left: SELECT dm.emp_no, dm.dept_no, dm.from_date FROM dept_manager AS dm JOIN departments AS d ON dm.dept_no = d.dept_no
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, dept_no, from_date FROM dept_manager

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without departments' key two departments may share a number, and the join repeats the manager row
pairs.left: SELECT dm.emp_no, dm.dept_no, dm.from_date FROM dept_manager AS dm JOIN departments AS d ON dm.dept_no = d.dept_no
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, dept_no, from_date FROM dept_manager

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: the join is no longer the identity once the parent is filtered: assignments of male employees are lost
pairs.left: SELECT de.emp_no, de.dept_no FROM dept_emp AS de JOIN employees AS e ON de.emp_no = e.emp_no WHERE de.emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200 AND e.gender = 'F'
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, dept_no FROM dept_emp WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: departments is joined on its primary key, so each assignment matches at most one row and none is lost
pairs.left: SELECT de.emp_no, de.dept_no FROM dept_emp AS de LEFT JOIN departments AS d ON de.dept_no = d.dept_no WHERE de.emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, dept_no FROM dept_emp WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without departments' key a department number may repeat, and the left join repeats the assignment
pairs.left: SELECT de.emp_no, de.dept_no FROM dept_emp AS de LEFT JOIN departments AS d ON de.dept_no = d.dept_no WHERE de.emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, dept_no FROM dept_emp WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: dept_manager is joined on both columns of its composite primary key (emp_no, dept_no): at most one match per row
pairs.left: SELECT de.emp_no, de.dept_no FROM dept_emp AS de LEFT JOIN dept_manager AS dm ON dm.emp_no = de.emp_no AND dm.dept_no = de.dept_no
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, dept_no FROM dept_emp

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: dept_no is only part of dept_manager's key: a department with several managers repeats the assignment
pairs.left: SELECT de.emp_no, de.dept_no FROM dept_emp AS de LEFT JOIN dept_manager AS dm ON dm.dept_no = de.dept_no WHERE de.emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, dept_no FROM dept_emp WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without dept_manager's key the same (employee, department) may appear twice, with different dates
pairs.left: SELECT de.emp_no, de.dept_no FROM dept_emp AS de LEFT JOIN dept_manager AS dm ON dm.emp_no = de.emp_no AND dm.dept_no = de.dept_no
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, dept_no FROM dept_emp

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: the filter rejects NULL, so the rows the left join pads are removed again and the join is an inner join
pairs.left: SELECT e.emp_no, dm.from_date FROM employees AS e LEFT JOIN dept_manager AS dm ON dm.emp_no = e.emp_no WHERE dm.from_date > DATE '1990-01-01'
pairs.right: SELECT e.emp_no, dm.from_date FROM employees AS e JOIN dept_manager AS dm ON dm.emp_no = e.emp_no WHERE dm.from_date > DATE '1990-01-01'

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: the filter accepts the NULLs of unmatched employees, which the inner join does not produce
pairs.left: SELECT e.emp_no, dm.from_date FROM employees AS e LEFT JOIN dept_manager AS dm ON dm.emp_no = e.emp_no WHERE dm.from_date > DATE '1990-01-01' OR dm.from_date IS NULL
pairs.right: SELECT e.emp_no, dm.from_date FROM employees AS e JOIN dept_manager AS dm ON dm.emp_no = e.emp_no WHERE dm.from_date > DATE '1990-01-01' OR dm.from_date IS NULL

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: the join is on all three columns of titles' primary key (emp_no, title, from_date), one DATE among them: each row meets only itself
pairs.left: SELECT t1.emp_no, t1.title, t1.from_date FROM titles AS t1 JOIN titles AS t2 ON t1.emp_no = t2.emp_no AND t1.title = t2.title AND t1.from_date = t2.from_date WHERE t1.emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, title, from_date FROM titles WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without from_date the join pairs two stints of the same title of one employee, so the row repeats
pairs.left: SELECT t1.emp_no, t1.title, t1.from_date FROM titles AS t1 JOIN titles AS t2 ON t1.emp_no = t2.emp_no AND t1.title = t2.title WHERE t1.emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, title, from_date FROM titles WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: the join is on salaries' whole primary key (emp_no, from_date)
pairs.left: SELECT s1.emp_no, s1.from_date, s1.salary FROM salaries AS s1 JOIN salaries AS s2 ON s1.emp_no = s2.emp_no AND s1.from_date = s2.from_date WHERE s1.emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, from_date, salary FROM salaries WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: emp_no alone is not salaries' key: an employee with several salary periods is paired with each of them
pairs.left: SELECT s1.emp_no, s1.from_date, s1.salary FROM salaries AS s1 JOIN salaries AS s2 ON s1.emp_no = s2.emp_no WHERE s1.emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10040
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, from_date, salary FROM salaries WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10040

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without salaries' key the same (employee, start date) may be stored twice
pairs.left: SELECT s1.emp_no, s1.from_date, s1.salary FROM salaries AS s1 JOIN salaries AS s2 ON s1.emp_no = s2.emp_no AND s1.from_date = s2.from_date WHERE s1.emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, from_date, salary FROM salaries WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: emp_no is employees' primary key, so no two rows are equal
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT emp_no, last_name FROM employees
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, last_name FROM employees

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: last names repeat across employees
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT last_name, gender FROM employees
pairs.right: SELECT last_name, gender FROM employees

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the primary key the same employee row may be stored twice
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT emp_no, last_name FROM employees
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, last_name FROM employees

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: (emp_no, dept_no) is dept_emp's primary key and these columns contain it
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT dept_no, emp_no, from_date FROM dept_emp WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200
pairs.right: SELECT dept_no, emp_no, from_date FROM dept_emp WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: dept_no alone repeats: many employees work in a department
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT dept_no FROM dept_emp WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200
pairs.right: SELECT dept_no FROM dept_emp WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: titles' primary key is (emp_no, title, from_date): the DATE is a key column
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT emp_no, title, from_date FROM titles WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, title, from_date FROM titles WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without from_date two stints of the same title of one employee are equal rows
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT emp_no, title FROM titles WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, title FROM titles WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: (emp_no, from_date) is not titles' key: the title is part of it, so one employee may start two titles on one day
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT emp_no, from_date FROM titles WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, from_date FROM titles WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: salaries' primary key is (emp_no, from_date)
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT emp_no, from_date, salary FROM salaries WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, from_date, salary FROM salaries WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: an employee can be paid the same salary in two periods
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT emp_no, salary FROM salaries WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, salary FROM salaries WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: DISTINCT on the key of the outer table undoes the fan-out of the join: each employee once if any assignment exists
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT e.emp_no, e.last_name FROM employees AS e JOIN dept_emp AS de ON de.emp_no = e.emp_no WHERE e.emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200
pairs.right: SELECT e.emp_no, e.last_name FROM employees AS e WHERE e.emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dept_emp AS de WHERE de.emp_no = e.emp_no)

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: an employee with two department assignments appears twice in the join
pairs.left: SELECT e.emp_no, e.last_name FROM employees AS e JOIN dept_emp AS de ON de.emp_no = e.emp_no WHERE e.emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200
pairs.right: SELECT e.emp_no, e.last_name FROM employees AS e WHERE e.emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dept_emp AS de WHERE de.emp_no = e.emp_no)

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: titles.from_date is NOT NULL
pairs.left: SELECT COUNT(from_date) FROM titles
pairs.right: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM titles

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: titles.to_date is nullable (the one nullable column of the database)
pairs.left: SELECT COUNT(to_date) FROM titles
pairs.right: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM titles

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: emp_no is employees' primary key
pairs.left: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT emp_no) FROM employees
pairs.right: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM employees

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: emp_no repeats in salaries: one row per salary period
pairs.left: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT emp_no) FROM salaries
pairs.right: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM salaries

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: hire_date depends on the key emp_no, so adding it to the grouping does not split a group
pairs.left: SELECT e.emp_no, e.last_name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM employees AS e JOIN dept_emp AS de ON de.emp_no = e.emp_no WHERE e.emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200 GROUP BY e.emp_no, e.last_name, e.hire_date
pairs.right: SELECT e.emp_no, e.last_name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM employees AS e JOIN dept_emp AS de ON de.emp_no = e.emp_no WHERE e.emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200 GROUP BY e.emp_no, e.last_name

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: to_date does not depend on emp_no: an employee's salary periods end on different days
pairs.left: SELECT s.emp_no, COUNT(*) AS n FROM salaries AS s WHERE s.emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200 GROUP BY s.emp_no, s.to_date
pairs.right: SELECT s.emp_no, COUNT(*) AS n FROM salaries AS s WHERE s.emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200 GROUP BY s.emp_no

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: grouping by salaries' whole primary key makes each group one row, and the sum of one NOT NULL value is that value
pairs.left: SELECT emp_no, from_date, SUM(salary) AS salary FROM salaries WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200 GROUP BY emp_no, from_date
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, from_date, salary FROM salaries WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: one group per employee, not per salary period
pairs.left: SELECT emp_no, SUM(salary) AS salary FROM salaries WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200 GROUP BY emp_no
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, salary FROM salaries WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: a condition on the group key filters whole groups, before or after grouping
pairs.left: SELECT dept_no, COUNT(*) AS n FROM dept_emp GROUP BY dept_no HAVING dept_no <> 'd005'
pairs.right: SELECT dept_no, COUNT(*) AS n FROM dept_emp WHERE dept_no <> 'd005' GROUP BY dept_no

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: a department whose assignments have all ended is a group with count 0 in one query and no group in the other
pairs.left: SELECT dept_no, COUNT(*) AS n FROM dept_emp WHERE to_date = DATE '9999-01-01' GROUP BY dept_no
pairs.right: SELECT dept_no, COUNTIF(to_date = DATE '9999-01-01') AS n FROM dept_emp GROUP BY dept_no

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: a filter on the grouping column can run before the aggregate
pairs.left: SELECT * FROM (SELECT emp_no, COUNT(*) AS n FROM salaries GROUP BY emp_no) WHERE emp_no = 10001
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, COUNT(*) AS n FROM salaries WHERE emp_no = 10001 GROUP BY emp_no

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: grouping by departments' key keeps one row per department with its count of matches, as the correlated count does
pairs.left: SELECT d.dept_no, COUNT(dm.emp_no) AS managers FROM departments AS d LEFT JOIN dept_manager AS dm ON dm.dept_no = d.dept_no GROUP BY d.dept_no
pairs.right: SELECT d.dept_no, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dept_manager AS dm WHERE dm.dept_no = d.dept_no) AS managers FROM departments AS d

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without departments' key a department number may repeat: one query merges the two rows into one group, the other keeps both
pairs.left: SELECT d.dept_no, COUNT(dm.emp_no) AS managers FROM departments AS d LEFT JOIN dept_manager AS dm ON dm.dept_no = d.dept_no GROUP BY d.dept_no
pairs.right: SELECT d.dept_no, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dept_manager AS dm WHERE dm.dept_no = d.dept_no) AS managers FROM departments AS d

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: IN over a subquery is a semi join, as EXISTS is
pairs.left: SELECT emp_no FROM employees WHERE emp_no IN (SELECT emp_no FROM dept_manager WHERE from_date > DATE '1990-01-01')
pairs.right: SELECT e.emp_no FROM employees AS e WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dept_manager AS dm WHERE dm.emp_no = e.emp_no AND dm.from_date > DATE '1990-01-01')

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: an employee in two departments is listed twice by the join and once by IN
pairs.left: SELECT e.emp_no FROM employees AS e JOIN dept_emp AS de ON de.emp_no = e.emp_no WHERE e.emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no FROM employees WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200 AND emp_no IN (SELECT emp_no FROM dept_emp)

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: departments' key makes the join return at most one row per assignment, so it filters like IN
pairs.left: SELECT de.emp_no FROM dept_emp AS de WHERE de.emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200 AND de.dept_no IN (SELECT dept_no FROM departments WHERE dept_name = 'Sales')
pairs.right: SELECT de.emp_no FROM dept_emp AS de JOIN departments AS d ON d.dept_no = de.dept_no WHERE de.emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200 AND d.dept_name = 'Sales'

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without departments' key two 'Sales' rows with one number repeat the assignment in the join
pairs.left: SELECT de.emp_no FROM dept_emp AS de WHERE de.emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200 AND de.dept_no IN (SELECT dept_no FROM departments WHERE dept_name = 'Sales')
pairs.right: SELECT de.emp_no FROM dept_emp AS de JOIN departments AS d ON d.dept_no = de.dept_no WHERE de.emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200 AND d.dept_name = 'Sales'

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: dept_manager.emp_no is NOT NULL, so NOT IN has no NULL to turn the answer unknown
pairs.left: SELECT emp_no FROM employees WHERE emp_no NOT IN (SELECT emp_no FROM dept_manager)
pairs.right: SELECT e.emp_no FROM employees AS e WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dept_manager AS dm WHERE dm.emp_no = e.emp_no)

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: titles.to_date is nullable: one NULL makes NOT IN return nothing, while NOT EXISTS still returns the rows
pairs.left: SELECT s.emp_no FROM salaries AS s WHERE s.emp_no < 10100 AND s.to_date NOT IN (SELECT t.to_date FROM titles AS t)
pairs.right: SELECT s.emp_no FROM salaries AS s WHERE s.emp_no < 10100 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM titles AS t WHERE t.to_date = s.to_date)

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: both DATE columns are NOT NULL
pairs.left: SELECT e.emp_no FROM employees AS e WHERE e.hire_date NOT IN (SELECT de.to_date FROM dept_emp AS de)
pairs.right: SELECT e.emp_no FROM employees AS e WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dept_emp AS de WHERE de.to_date = e.hire_date)

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without NOT NULL on dept_emp.to_date a NULL end date empties the NOT IN
pairs.left: SELECT e.emp_no FROM employees AS e WHERE e.hire_date NOT IN (SELECT de.to_date FROM dept_emp AS de)
pairs.right: SELECT e.emp_no FROM employees AS e WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dept_emp AS de WHERE de.to_date = e.hire_date)

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: DISTINCT on departments' key turns the join back into a semi join
pairs.left: SELECT d.dept_no FROM departments AS d WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dept_manager AS dm WHERE dm.dept_no = d.dept_no)
pairs.right: SELECT DISTINCT d.dept_no FROM departments AS d JOIN dept_manager AS dm ON dm.dept_no = d.dept_no

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: a department with two managers over time is listed twice by the join
pairs.left: SELECT d.dept_no FROM departments AS d WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dept_manager AS dm WHERE dm.dept_no = d.dept_no)
pairs.right: SELECT d.dept_no FROM departments AS d JOIN dept_manager AS dm ON dm.dept_no = d.dept_no

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: an employee in both tables is kept twice by UNION ALL and once by UNION DISTINCT
pairs.left: SELECT emp_no FROM dept_emp WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200 UNION ALL SELECT emp_no FROM titles WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no FROM dept_emp WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200 UNION DISTINCT SELECT emp_no FROM titles WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: gender is NOT NULL, so the two filters split the table
pairs.left: SELECT emp_no FROM employees WHERE gender = 'M' UNION ALL SELECT emp_no FROM employees WHERE gender <> 'M'
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no FROM employees

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: a title with a NULL to_date is in neither half
pairs.left: SELECT emp_no FROM titles WHERE to_date > DATE '1995-01-01' UNION ALL SELECT emp_no FROM titles WHERE to_date <= DATE '1995-01-01'
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no FROM titles

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: INTERSECT DISTINCT is a de-duplicated semi join
pairs.left: SELECT emp_no FROM dept_emp INTERSECT DISTINCT SELECT emp_no FROM dept_manager
pairs.right: SELECT DISTINCT de.emp_no FROM dept_emp AS de WHERE de.emp_no IN (SELECT emp_no FROM dept_manager)

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: INTERSECT treats two NULLs as equal and IN does not: titles.to_date is nullable
pairs.left: SELECT to_date FROM titles WHERE emp_no < 10100 INTERSECT DISTINCT SELECT to_date FROM titles WHERE emp_no >= 10100
pairs.right: SELECT DISTINCT t.to_date FROM titles AS t WHERE t.emp_no < 10100 AND t.to_date IN (SELECT to_date FROM titles WHERE emp_no >= 10100)

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: employees.birth_date is NOT NULL
pairs.left: SELECT emp_no FROM employees WHERE birth_date IS NULL
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no FROM employees WHERE FALSE

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: titles.to_date may be NULL
pairs.left: SELECT emp_no FROM titles WHERE to_date IS NULL
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no FROM titles WHERE FALSE

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: salaries.to_date is NOT NULL, so COALESCE returns it
pairs.left: SELECT emp_no, COALESCE(to_date, DATE '9999-01-01') AS to_date FROM salaries WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, to_date FROM salaries WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: titles.to_date may be NULL, which the COALESCE replaces by the open-ended sentinel
pairs.left: SELECT emp_no, COALESCE(to_date, DATE '9999-01-01') AS to_date FROM titles WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, to_date FROM titles WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: gender is NOT NULL, so NOT (a = b) and a <> b agree
pairs.left: SELECT emp_no FROM employees WHERE NOT (gender = 'F')
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no FROM employees WHERE gender <> 'F'

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: for a NULL to_date the negated comparison is unknown, so the row is dropped, while the second query keeps it
pairs.left: SELECT emp_no FROM titles WHERE NOT (to_date = DATE '9999-01-01')
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no FROM titles WHERE to_date <> DATE '9999-01-01' OR to_date IS NULL

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: a year is the half-open range from its first day to the first day of the next year
pairs.left: SELECT emp_no FROM employees WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM hire_date) = 1990
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no FROM employees WHERE hire_date >= DATE '1990-01-01' AND hire_date < DATE '1991-01-01'

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: the closed range includes the first day of 1991
pairs.left: SELECT emp_no FROM employees WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM hire_date) = 1990
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no FROM employees WHERE hire_date >= DATE '1990-01-01' AND hire_date <= DATE '1991-01-01'

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: BETWEEN is inclusive at both ends
pairs.left: SELECT emp_no, from_date FROM salaries WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200 AND from_date BETWEEN DATE '1990-01-01' AND DATE '1995-12-31'
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, from_date FROM salaries WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200 AND from_date >= DATE '1990-01-01' AND from_date <= DATE '1995-12-31'

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: a salary that starts on 1995-12-31 is lost by the exclusive end
pairs.left: SELECT emp_no, from_date FROM salaries WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200 AND from_date BETWEEN DATE '1990-01-01' AND DATE '1995-12-31'
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, from_date FROM salaries WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200 AND from_date >= DATE '1990-01-01' AND from_date < DATE '1995-12-31'

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: the only day after 9998-12-31 and not after 9999-01-01 is 9999-01-01 itself
pairs.left: SELECT emp_no, salary FROM salaries WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200 AND to_date = DATE '9999-01-01'
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, salary FROM salaries WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200 AND to_date > DATE '9998-12-31' AND to_date <= DATE '9999-01-01'

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: DATE reaches 9999-12-31: a period ending in June 9999 is open-ended by the second test only
pairs.left: SELECT emp_no, salary FROM salaries WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200 AND to_date = DATE '9999-01-01'
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, salary FROM salaries WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10200 AND to_date >= DATE '9999-01-01'

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: a filter on the partition column removes whole partitions only, so the ranks inside the others are unchanged
pairs.left: SELECT emp_no, dept_no, r FROM (SELECT emp_no, dept_no, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY dept_no ORDER BY from_date) AS r FROM dept_emp) WHERE dept_no = 'd005' AND emp_no < 10100
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, dept_no, r FROM (SELECT emp_no, dept_no, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY dept_no ORDER BY from_date) AS r FROM dept_emp WHERE dept_no = 'd005') WHERE emp_no < 10100

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: filtering on emp_no before ranking removes rows from the partitions and changes the ranks of the others
pairs.left: SELECT emp_no, dept_no, r FROM (SELECT emp_no, dept_no, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY dept_no ORDER BY from_date) AS r FROM dept_emp) WHERE emp_no < 10100
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no, dept_no, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY dept_no ORDER BY from_date) AS r FROM dept_emp WHERE emp_no < 10100
